title: PRD: Hosted Mixed-Surface scope clarification and launch checksheet (chat / completions / embeddings / rerank)
creator: Ava Patel
description: Purpose: Clarify the scope, behavioral contracts, and acceptance gates for a bundled hosted surface that exposes chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank under a single product offering. This ticket consolidates remaining open decisions, records explicit endpoint compatibility requirements, and produces a launch checksheet that ops/QA/SRE can follow during staged rollouts. The output of this ticket is a finalized PRD section used by engineering to implement compatibility adapters, plus a deterministic acceptance and launch checksheet for the release runbook.
goals: Define precise behavioral guarantees for each surface (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank) when routed through the single hosted endpoint adapter.
Agree on deterministic fallbacks and quality bands for progressive rollouts to minimize customer-facing regressions.
Produce a launch checksheet with measurable SLOs, telemetry hooks, and rollout gates for canary → ramp → GA.
Document compatibility requirements so client SDKs and product docs can be updated in one coordinated release.
out_of_scope: Large-scale model onboarding (separate onboarding PRDs exist).
Dedicated or Private deployment variations — this ticket targets the hosted API only.
Billing model changes (pricing/quotas are handled by Finance track).
requirements: Routing: single request-level selector must map incoming requests to an explicit surface type: chat, completion, embedding, rerank. If surface is omitted, default to 'completion' and emit a deprecation warning header for 3 months.

Behavioral Contracts: chat must support conversation state (conversation_id + message refs) and streaming; completions must support stop tokens, max_tokens, and sampling temperature semantics consistent with existing hosted endpoints; embeddings must accept batched inputs up to 512 items and return vector length aligned with model vector_size; rerank must accept an ordered list of documents and a query payload and return normalized scores and stable tie-break behavior.
Backward compatibility: existing clients using legacy endpoint names must be supported with a compatibility adapter for 6 months and rate-limited at parity with current quotas.

Observability: token-level latency, model-selection histogram, error-class breakdown, and per-route quality-signal (for generation: BLEU/ROUGE proxies; for embeddings: similarity drift) must be emitted to telemetry with tags: surface, model_variant, region, lane.
Safety and guardrails: annotate responses with safety metadata when detection heuristics fire; outbound PII redaction must be togglable per-tenant and default off for public beta.

Rollout controls: implement a graded-fallback governor allowing automatic switch from model_variant_A → model_variant_B on sustained QoS degradation (latency p95 > 2s or error_rate > 0.5%) and a manual kill switch in the console.
E2E: end-to-end sample harness that runs 500 synthetic prompts per surface type and compares outputs against golden-set thresholds for quality regressions before any canary traffic expansion.
acceptance_criteria: Functional: Each surface type passes the E2E harness with quality metrics within tolerance (generation quality within -3% to +inf compared to baseline; embedding cosine similarity distribution shift < 1.5% mean), and all API contracts validated by integration tests.

Reliability: Canary cluster achieves at least 99.5% success rate for 24 hours with p95 latency below configured SLOs (generations p95 < 700ms for small models; embeddings p95 < 1200ms for batched 128 items).
Compatibility: Legacy endpoint traffic routed through compatibility adapter shows no more than 0.2% error delta vs historical baseline and logs deprecation header for 3 months.
Observability: Telemetry dashboards populated with required metrics and at least three predefined alert rules (latency SLO breach, quality regression spike, model-selection mismatch).
Security: Security review signed off and KMS integration validated for model-specific encryption keys when customer-provided keys are used.
Docs & SDK: SDKs updated with the new unified surface examples for all four surfaces, and doc snippets validated by developer-advocate smoke tests.
Ops: Launch checksheet executed in staging with checklist items marked, runbook created for rollback and emergency fallback to older hosted bundle.
rollout_plan: Step 0 (Prep): Merge compatibility adapter and observational hooks. Run integration suite. Create a staging workspace mirroring production traffic slices.
Step 1 (Smoke): Enable on 0.1% of production traffic (internal + dogfood accounts) for 12 hours. Monitor error rate, p95 latency, and quality probes. Hold if any metric breaches gate thresholds.

Step 2 (Canary): Expand to 2% for 48 hours. Run full E2E harness continuously. If quality regression > 1% or latency SLO breaches for >2 hours, trigger automatic rollback to previous model_variant and page on-call.
Step 3 (Ramp): Gradually increase traffic to 25% over 3 days with staged ramping and manual review checkpoints at 5% and 15%.
Step 4 (GA): After 7 days of stable canary + ramp, open GA release, create customer communications notes, and mark deprecation timelines for legacy endpoints.
launch_checklist: PRD signoff from PM, Eng (runtime + SDK + infra), Design (API samples), Security and Legal.
All integration and regression tests green in main branch for both content and telemetry flows.
Telemetry dashboards created: surface performance, model selection, quality drift, errors_by_type.
SLOs and alert thresholds configured in PagerDuty/Alerting system.
E2E golden-set harness executed on canary cluster and results attached to the release ticket.
Compatibility adapter validated with legacy client replay for a 48-hour window.
Docs: Developer guide updated, OpenAPI spec published, SDK packages published to internal npm/pypi with sample snippets.
Console: rollout control toggles and manual kill switch validated by SRE in staging.
Security: KMS integration smoke test (encrypt/decrypt per-tenant) completed, security sign-off attached.
Support: Support playbook and known-issues KB created, support rotation briefed, runbook for rollback uploaded to runbooks folder.
Legal/Compliance: Data residency and retention notes verified for regionally regulated tenants included in release notes.
Post-launch: Plan for 48/72/168-hour postmortem checks scheduled and assigned.
risks_mitigations: Risk: Quality regression for generation when model variants differ in tokenization or sampling. Mitigation: include token-level parity tests and a conservative sampling fallback that preserves previous behavior during rollout.

Risk: Embedding vector-size mismatch across model variants. Mitigation: enforce schema validation in adapter and fail fast with clear error for mismatched vector sizes; provide auto-migration guidance if model change required.
Risk: Increased per-token latency from unified routing overhead. Mitigation: microbench routing path and add an opt-in 'fast-path' header for high-SLA customers during early usage.
Risk: Customers notice changed surface semantics. Mitigation: emit deprecation headers, staged docs, and targeted customer outreach for top 20 tenants before GA.
notes: Decision: default_empty_surface -> 'completion' chosen to minimize breakage; deprecation window set to 90 days.
Tradeoff: enabling PII redaction by default blocks some analytic use cases; default left off for beta to reduce false positives and allow tenants to opt-in.
Follow-up: separate ticket to instrument per-tenant quality baselining (PM-991200) created to improve future auto-roll decisions.
